external_entities.name: duty engineers
external_entities.description: Engineers who use the dispatch console from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state how engineers authenticate to the console.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work through a SOAP feed.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state how the partner identifies the importer.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript application used by duty engineers and connected to the dispatch API, including a WebSocket for live job status.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.
processes.notes: The source does not state how an engineer signs in to the console. CORS configuration is undocumented, including allowed origins and credential support.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer; it reads and writes the dispatch database and runs in the production control plane.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
processes.notes: The source does not state the API's authentication mechanism for the console. The API answers the console cross-origin, but allowed origins and credential support are undocumented.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: An hourly importer that pulls and parses the scheduling partner's SOAP XML feed, archives downloaded documents, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The source does not state how the importer identifies the scheduling partner. The API token was issued when the importer was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: Database containing job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order carries the token or session that created it, but nothing about the person behind that token. Protection at rest is undocumented.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder where the importer writes each XML document downloaded from the scheduling partner.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_stores.notes: The source describes this as a folder on the corporate file store but does not state its separate trust-zone placement or protection at rest.

data_stores.name: corporate file store
data_stores.description: The corporate file store containing the schedule archive folder.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store
data_stores.notes: The source does not state what other data the file store contains or how it is protected at rest.

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: Duty engineers open the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: serve console
data_flows.description: The corporate web host serves the dispatch console application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API cross-origin.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The console and API are served from different origins. The API answers cross-origin, but the allowed origins and credential setting are undocumented.
data_flows.data_description: dispatch console API requests and responses

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state whether the socket uses TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether the engineer's session is checked again after opening.

data_flows.name: read and write dispatch data
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: publish planned work
data_flows.description: The scheduling partner publishes tomorrow's planned work to the schedule importer through a SOAP feed over HTTPS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: The source does not state how the partner identifies the importer or how the importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write schedule document
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: The importer presents an API token. The token was issued when the importer was built and has not been rotated.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers are located and the schedule importer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company control plane holding the live estate, with authority to move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet. A corporate laptop holds none of the control-plane rights.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The separate company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API is internally exposed because its production control plane is not reachable from the internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the dispatch API runs in the production control plane and that the control plane is not reachable from the internet.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database is confidential because it contains crew mobile numbers, job orders, and creating tokens or sessions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database holds job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule archive is confidential because it contains tomorrow's planned work downloaded from the scheduling partner.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the importer writes downloaded schedule documents containing tomorrow's planned work into the schedule archive.
